{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|US Cuisine]]

'''Chicken parmigiana''' is a popular [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]]-[[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American]] dish served in a variety of ways. The same basic recipe works for a number of dishes. The components usually consists of a breaded, tenderized piece of [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] (or slice of [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]]), a simple [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]], and [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (usually [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]]). A thicker [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]], such as linguini, a toasted loaf of Italian [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], and a light red wine such as Chianti complement this dish well.

This recipe is typical of the parmigiana recipes from New York and New Jersey.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 teaspoon of [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ a teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* ¼ teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* ¼ teaspoon of finely-crushed [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* ½ a [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato puree]]
* ¼ cup of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]] (see below if you wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]])
* ½ a cup of shredded [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
* ¼ a cup of grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano cheese]]

==Procedure==
#In a heavy [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] (preferably cast iron), heat the oil on medium heat.
#While the oil is heating, use a tenderizing mallet (or the ball of your hand) to pound the chicken breasts to about ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick. This step is important to ensure the chicken is tender and more importantly to ensure the chicken cooks thoroughly.
# Season the chicken breasts with salt and garlic powder.
# [[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] the breasts in flour and shake off any excess.
# Place both breasts in the heated oil for 3 minutes, then flip and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for an additional 2 minutes.
# Remove the breasts and place on a rack or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]].
# Preheat a [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]].
# In a large oven-safe [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the tomato puree and chicken stock until it begins to [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmer]].
# Add the oregano, basil, and pepper to saucepan and mix
# Place cooked chicken breasts in pan and flip a number of times to coat with sauce.
# Add mozzarella and parmigiana cheese to the tops of the breasts.
# Broil for 30–60 seconds. It will burn very quickly, so check it frequently.
# Remove from oven and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Use thin-sliced chicken cutlets (available at most supermarkets) to avoid the BIG mess and time of pounding.
* If [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] is to be served with this meal, it should be timed so that the parmigiana is done right when the pasta is. The pasta should be removed directly from the pot and placed into the pan. The remaining sauce can then be used with the pasta.
* This recipe works best with breasts that come from slightly older chickens (such as broiler or fryer chickens). These chickens have a stronger taste but are generally tougher.  The tenderizing step takes care of the toughness of the older birds though.
* If you do not live in area where fresh tomatoes are grown, canned tomatoes are usually superior to the low-cost ones you will find in the supermarket.

* For [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] parmigiana, follow the same steps except do not tenderize.  Veal is already tender enough.  The veal can also be cooked for 2 minutes on each side.
* Omit the tenderizing step for [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] parmigiana.
* If you want to use fresh garlic instead of powder, add it to the sauce instead of adding it to the chicken breast.
* You can also try using other types of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheeses]] such as [[Cookbook:Provolone Cheese|provolone cheese]] or [[Cookbook:Fontina Cheese|fontina cheese]] to add more of a "tasty kick" compared to a mild cheese like mozzarella 
* You may wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. When frying with olive oil, be sure to use a cheap solvent-extracted grade! The fancy grades can not tolerate heat. They have [[Cookbook:Smoke Point|smoke points]] as low as 200°F (93°C), making for both a fire hazard and a source of smoke. Save the cold-pressed extra-virgin olive oil for a [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]].
